6577.t: Uncertain. According to Beekes, probably from Pre-Greek.

6532.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₁ésti. Cognate with Sanskrit अस्ति॑ (ásti), Latin est, Old Persian 𐎠𐎿𐎫𐎡𐎹 (astiy), Hittite 𒂊𒌍𒍣 (ēszi), Old Church Slavonic єстъ (estŭ), Gothic 𐌹𐍃𐍄 (ist).

6568.t: From earlier *ϝέσνυμαι (*wésnumai), from Proto-Indo-European *wes- (“to dress”). Particularly close cognate with Old Armenian զգենում (zgenum, “to dress oneself”).

6569.t: PIE word *wek⁽ʷ⁾speros From Proto-Hellenic *wésperos, from Proto-Indo-European *wek⁽ʷ⁾speros (“evening”). Cognates include Latin vesper, Old Armenian գիշեր (gišer), and Old Church Slavonic вєчєръ (večerŭ).

6558.t: Neuter substantive of *ἔντερος (*énteros, “inside”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₁énteros, from *h₁én (whence also ἐν (en, “in”)) + *-teros (whence also -τερος (-teros, “comparative suffix”)).

6561.t: Uhlenbeck and others consider it cognate with Sanskrit रम॑ते (rámate, “to calm down; to enjoy; to have sex with”), Lithuanian rimti (“calm down”), Gothic 𐍂𐌹𐌼𐌹𐍃 (rimis, “tranquility”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₁rem-; the Greek could then be from a…

6566.t: PIE word *swé Apparently from Proto-Hellenic *hwe = *ϝ̔έ (*whé), from Proto-Indo-European *swé (reflexive pronoun).

6562.t: From Proto-Hellenic *wérd͏̌ō, from Proto-Indo-European *wérǵ-ye-, a *ye-present from the root *werǵ-, the same root as ῥέζω (rhézō) and ἔργον (érgon).

6574.t: According to Beekes from Proto-Indo-European *h₂em- (“to grasp”) and cognate with Latin ānsa (“handle”) and Lithuanian ąsà (“handle”).

6545.t: From ἐν- (en-) + γίγνομαι (gígnomai) + -ος (-os). Compare Latin indigenus (“native, indigenous”) and Primitive Irish ᚔᚅᚔᚌᚓᚅᚐ (inigena, “daughter”).

6565.t: PIE word *swé From Proto-Indo-European *swet-, from *swé (“self”). Cognate with Proto-Slavic *svatъ (“father of newlyweds”).

6584.t: From Proto-Indo-European *seykʷ- (“to filter”) and cognate with Old English sēon (“to filter”), Russian сцать (scatʹ, “to piss”) and Sanskrit सिञ्चति (siñcáti, “to pour”). Beekes suggests *seyk- as the original root.

6578.t: Unknown. Osthoff and Brugman connected this word to Latin sinō (“to permit, allow”) (assuming cognacy with Latin sēmen (“seed”)), but this is now viewed as impossible.

6539.t: From ἑλε- (hele-, “to take, capture”, aorist stem of αἱρέω (hairéō)) + πόλις (pólis, “city”): literally “taking or capturing cities”.

6599.t: Beekes reconstructs Proto-Indo-European *tḱiH-in (“kite”), connecting the word with Old Armenian ցին (cʻin, “kite”), Avestan 𐬯𐬀𐬉𐬥𐬀 (saēna, “a mythical bird”), and Sanskrit श्येन (śyena, “eagle, falcon”).

6585.t: Formation like ἀχλύς (akhlús) and δελφύς (delphús). Identical with Proto-Slavic *jьlъ (“silt; clay”) and Latvian īls (“very dark”).

6526.t: Analyzable as By surface analysis, ἐπι- (epĭ-) + κλῆσις (klêsĭs) or as ἐπικαλέω (epĭkăléō) + -σις (-sĭs).

6506.t: From ἐπι- (epi-, on, upon) + κρεμάννυμι (kremánnūmi, “to hang”).

6591.t: Traditionally derived from εἶμι (eîmĭ, “to be going to go”), which is from Proto-Indo-European *h₁ey-, though most other oxytones in -αμός (-ămós) are substantives (such as ποταμός (potămós)); Beekes suggests it comes from the Attic popular language.

6579.t: From ἡδύς (hēdús, “sweet”) + -ος (-os). Apparently originally an Aeolic form due to the loss of /h/.

6593.t: Per Schwyzer and Frisk, probably from an unattested noun *ἱδρυ- (*hidru-), a derivative in -ρ- (-r-) (comparing ἕδρα (hédra, “seat”)) of Proto-Indo-European *sed- (“to sit; settle”), also seen in ἕζομαι (hézomai, “to sit”) and ἵζω (hízō, “to sit, seat,…

6587.t: From ἰσο- (iso-, “equal, equivalent”) + δύναμις (dŭ́nămĭs, “force, power, strength, authority, value, meaning”) + -ος (-os, suffix forming second-declension compound adjectives).

6583.t: From ἴδιος (ĭ́dĭos, “one’s own; peculiar”) + -της (-tēs, abstract noun suffix).

6541.t: From ἑξακοσιοστός (hexăkosĭostós, “six hundred”) + -στός (-stós), a variant of -τός (-tós, ordinal suffix).
